Nov 25 : The Pittsburgh Steelers released four-times NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday after he claimed head coach Mike McCarthy is “unhealthy” and fell asleep during team meetings. Rodgers revealed he would not return to Pittsburgh during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” earlier on Wednesday, a day after he was benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. The 42-year-old previously said this season would be his last in the NFL. “At this point I'm not going back to Pittsburgh, that ship has sailed,” said Rodgers, who ranks third on the NFL’s all-time passing touchdowns list with 543.

He also described his past week with McCarthy, saying the 63-year-old head coach was "snoring" in a quarterback meeting and missed a couple other meetings and walk-throughs.  "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said.  Hours after Rodgers' remarks, Pittsburgh released the quarterback. Speaking to reporters later on Wednesday, McCarthy confirmed that benching Rodgers was his decision and said the team attempted to get in touch with the quarterback about it.  “Aaron and I have a long history,” McCarthy said. “He has a lot of opinions, and those are things we always talked about. Once again, I consider those private conversations.” Rodgers will be available to be claimed by any other team on waivers but would become an unrestricted free agent should he go unclaimed. ‘NAIL IN THE COFFIN’ Rodgers played 13 seasons under McCarthy with the Green Bay Packers, winning the Super Bowl after the 2010 season. In May he said McCarthy’s hiring played a role in his decision to return to Pittsburgh this season, adding on Wednesday that he “vouched” for McCarthy to be interviewed for the position. But he repeated that his breaking point with the coach came during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. "I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it, we're kind of on the offense on one side of defense on the other side. And there's some rambling or something and without even a heads up, he says, 'All right, one, two, three Packers'," Rodgers said. "That's what he broke it down on in the locker room."  McCarthy acknowledged the incident was an “embarrassing moment”. Rodgers said he had a conversation with McCarthy on Monday to address his concerns that date back to training camp. “We've had these conversations for months now and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy," Rodgers said. "If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy. If you’re not coming to everything you should be coming to as a playcaller." END OF AN ERA? Rodgers completed 220 of 361 passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions in 10 games for the 6-4 Steelers this season. If he has played his final NFL game, it would mark a sad ending to a glittering career for one of the league’s greatest ever quarterbacks. Rodgers dominated with the Packers from 2008 to 2022 before he was dealt to the New York Jets in a blockbuster trade in 2023. A season-ending Achilles tendon rupture tainted his first season with the Jets, and they posted a 5-12 record the following year.  In 2025 he signed a one-year deal with the Steelers, leading them to an AFC North title and playoff berth before they bowed out to the Houston Texans in a wild-card matchup. He signed another one-year contract with Steelers in May.

Source: Reuters

Nov 26 : Former Cricket Australia (CA) boss James Sutherland said on Thursday the governing body did the best it could with the information available to it during the investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The scandal was reignited this month after Usman Khawaja said the whole team had known about the ball-tampering plan during the tour of South Africa, not just the three players found culpable by CA's integrity unit. Batter Cameron Bancroft, one of the three players sanctioned, said last week he had witheld important details about the ball-tampering in order to avoid implicating others. "I don't look back on if things could, or should, have been dealt with differently," Sutherland, who stepped down in 2018, told the Herald Sun.

"We did the best we could with the situation that was in front of us and the information in front of us. It's a long time ago." Sutherland, now the CEO of Golf Australia, chose not to weigh in on the recent furore about the scandal. "I've made that personal commitment that I wouldn't make comments from afar on current cricket issues. I've been true to that so far," he told the Sydney Morning Herald. "It's fair to say it brings back some memories and not too many happy memories. I just recall it being an incredibly intense and stressful period." CA has ruled out another investigation, but last week attempted to draw a line under the scandal by announcing an independent forum for all the players to give their accounts without fear of sanction.

JAKARTA: Rescuers will resume the search on Thursday (Nov 26) for 13 workers trapped underground in an illegal gold mine in Indonesia's West Java province, with 13 already confirmed dead, police and rescue authorities said. In the region of Bogor, south of the capital Jakarta, a total of 26 workers entered the mine on Monday when heavy rains inundated the shaft and left them trapped 100m underground. Hengki, West Java's police chief, told Reuters that of the 13 fatalities, six have already been identified. The search would continue on Thursday barring bad weather conditions, he added. Access to the mine has been made more difficult by the narrow, slippery and dark conditions of the shaft, authorities said.

Indonesia's search and rescue agency (Basarnas) said rescuers were focusing on two mine shafts and were using ropes to gain access, but the 100m depth of the excavation complicated search efforts. Small-scale and illegal mining has caused a series of accidents in Indonesia, where mineral resources are located in remote areas in conditions that are difficult for authorities to regulate. In January, several miners were killed by carbon monoxide poisoning at an illegal gold mine in the same area, local news outlet Detik reported. State miner Antam, which runs gold mining operations in the region, said the incident occurred at an unauthorised mine and was not part of its operations.

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 26 : Australian business investment surged anew in the September quarter as firms poured money into data centres, recording its biggest rise since 2011 at the height of the mining boom, while companies further upgraded spending plans for coming months. The strong numbers on Thursday suggested some resilience in the Australian economy even as five interest rate hikes this year triggered the biggest housing downturn in 40 years, hit consumer spending and weakened the labour market. The local dollar rose 0.2 per cent to $0.6640 and three-year government bond futures reversed earlier gains to be down three ticks to 95.51. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported private capital spending jumped 12.2 per cent in the third quarter to an inflation-adjusted A$59.5 billion ($39.37 billion), far above market forecasts of a 4.4 per cent rise.  That was led by an 87 per cent jump in spending on information media and telecommunications equipment amid record investment in server racks and processing gear for data centres. Much of this was on imported equipment and thus an offsetting drag on economic growth.

Abhijit Surya, senior APAC economist at Capital Economics, said spending on information and communications technology could nearly double in the 2027 financial year, in contrast with the rest of the economy, where capital spending was struggling to tread water. "With the RBA clearly concerned about capacity pressures, the data suggest it won’t be in a rush to cut rates anytime soon," Surya said.  Markets are still wagering that the next move in interest rates will be down, but do not fully price a first cut from the Reserve Bank of Australia until August. A June cut is now seen as an 83 per cent chance. Overall spending on plant and machinery shot up 23.1 per cent, while spending on buildings and structures rose 1.7 per cent. FAST

BANGKOK: Thailand and Myanmar have agreed to establish six water-quality monitoring stations to investigate heavy-metal contamination in rivers along their shared border, Thai officials said on Wednesday (Nov 25), as concern over pollution grows in northern Thailand. A rash of mining activity in Myanmar, primarily to extract gold and rare earths, has led to the release of toxic chemicals into rivers flowing into Thailand, potentially contaminating water sources for communities, Reuters has reported. More than 2,400 mines - many of them illegal and unregulated - across mainland Southeast Asia could be releasing deadly chemicals such as cyanide and mercury into river water, according to the US-based Stimson Center think tank. Thailand's Pollution Control Department said tests from March to September 2025 detected arsenic and other heavy metals in water and sediment samples collected from the Kok River and its tributaries, as well as the Sai, Ruak and Mekong Rivers. The Kok flows from Myanmar's Shan State into Thailand's Chiang Rai province, while the Sai and Ruak form parts of the border.

At the first meeting of a Thai-Myanmar working group set up to tackle the pollution, both sides agreed to install four monitoring stations along the Kok River and two along the Sai River, according to a Thai government statement. "Both sides agreed to exchange water quality monitoring data through designated departments at least twice a year to facilitate regular information sharing and enhance coordination," the statement said. Thailand said on Sunday that it plans to stop exporting chemicals used in rare earth mining to Myanmar and designate its side of the Kok River a "pollution control zone" to tackle toxic contamination.

MINING IN MYANMAR'S SHAN STATE Thai investigations have focused on mining in war-torn Myanmar as a potential source of contamination, including areas in eastern Shan State under the control of a Chinese-backed militia, according to UN experts. In the remote hillsides of Shan State, Chinese miners opened new rare earth mines under the protection of the United Wa State Army militia group, Reuters reported last year. China said then that Chinese firms operating abroad are required to "abide by local laws and regulations and actively fulfill their social responsibilities".  Beijing has offered technical support, including information sharing, joint surveys and the establishment of a joint laboratory, said Raweewan Bhuridej, permanent secretary of Thailand's Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment. "China is prepared to support cooperation between Thailand and Myanmar," Raweewan said. Myanmar is one of the world's largest sources of rare earths that are primarily exported to China and turned into magnets that power critical goods like wind turbines, medical devices and electric vehicles. Key rare earth mining belts, including the Shan State areas bordering Thailand, are outside the control of Myanmar's military-backed government. The country has been ravaged by a nationwide civil war since a 2021 coup.

TOKYO, Nov 26 : The Bank of Japan must respond swiftly to signs of an inflation overshoot, including by accelerating the pace of interest rate hikes, hawkish board member Naoki Tamura said on Thursday, keeping alive prospects of a rate increase as soon as December. Rising raw material costs, including from higher crude oil prices due to the Middle East conflict, are already pushing up prices for a wide range of goods with the pass-through to consumer inflation seen intensifying ahead, Tamura said. "Recent price developments suggest further upside risks to inflation," he said, warning of price pressures from the Middle East war, higher import costs from a weak yen and still-robust demand for AI-related goods. "Given that financial conditions remain accommodative, I believe the BOJ needs to bring its policy rate to a level deemed neutral to the economy soon," Tamura said in a speech.

The remarks come ahead of the BOJ's two-day policy meeting ending on December 18, when markets widely expect the central bank to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent from the current 1.25 per cent. They also highlight the BOJ's focus on inflation risks, even as the recent market volatility and soft consumption cloud the outlook for Japan's fragile economy. Tamura said financial conditions remained accommodative with surveys suggesting the BOJ's past rate hikes, and potential future increases, were unlikely to inflict huge damage on corporate activity. "Within a few months of each rate hike, the BOJ can make a reasonable assessment of financial conditions" based on various surveys, Tamura said, signalling scope to follow up a rate hike in September with another one as soon as next month. "Given that underlying inflation in Japan is less firmly anchored at the BOJ's 2 per cent target, I believe the BOJ must respond swiftly to signs of an upward deviation in prices, including by accelerating the pace of policy interest rate hikes," he said. STILL SOME WAY TO NEUTRAL With high energy costs and the weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25 per cent in September after delivering a hike in June — a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes seen in 2024 and 2025.  The central bank kept rates steady in October, but said underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2 per cent target and signalled its readiness to continue hiking rates to prevent price growth from accelerating too much. Tamura did not mention an estimate he made in the past putting Japan's neutral rate, or the level that neither cools nor overheats the economy, around 2 per cent. But he said the BOJ's policy rate was "still some way" from neutral when judging from still-loose financial conditions. The need for further rate hikes is heightened by the fact Japan's inflation expectations are less firmly anchored than in other economies, leaving underlying inflation more vulnerable to large swings from external shocks, he said. "In my view, the BOJ therefore must respond to shocks more swiftly and strongly than would be necessary if underlying inflation were anchored more firmly." A former commercial bank executive, Tamura, along with former bond strategist Hajime Takata, is seen by markets as among the hawks on the nine-member board who prefer to hike rates steadily to forestall the risk of too-high inflation.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Nov 26 : The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate on Thursday, resuming its tightening cycle and upgrading its 2027 growth outlook to the fastest in six years amid a chip-driven export boom and persistent inflation. The move aligns the BOK with other emerging market economies, which are grappling with persistent commodity and supply pressures linked to the war in the Middle East. The seven-member monetary policy board voted to raise the 7-day repurchase rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.25 per cent, its highest since November 2024, a decision forecast by 32 of 34 analysts surveyed by Reuters. The bank also raised this year's growth forecast to 3.9 per cent from 3.3 per cent previously, and took its August outlook of 2.9 per cent for next year to 4.1 per cent, the fastest since 2021.

South Korea's policy-sensitive three-year treasury bond futures extended losses after the policy statement, falling 0.24 points to 103.77. The bank also saw stickier inflation for 2027, at 2.4 per cent, up from 2.3 per cent previously. "The central bank’s main concern is inflation, which has remained above its 2 per cent target since the conflict in Iran began – it came in at 2.8 per cent from a year ago in October," Gareth Leather, an analyst at Capital Economics, said after the rate decision. "Rapidly rising property prices, particularly in Seoul, could strengthen the case for a more prolonged tightening cycle." The hike was the BOK's third this year, following back-to-back increases in July and August, and brought cumulative tightening to 75 basis points. Asia's fourth-largest economy has expanded faster than anticipated in 2026 on surging global demand for semiconductors. Policymakers remained on a hawkish footing due to a heated housing market and headline inflation hovering well above the BOK's 2 per cent target. At its previous meeting on October 22, the central bank held rates steady at 3.00 per cent to assess external risks and the lagging impact of its summer hikes, while sharply upgrading its economic growth projections for both this year and next. BOK Governor Shin Hyun Song, who last month said the bank will take a data-dependent approach rather than a fixed rate trajectory, is scheduled to hold a news conference at 0210 GMT to explain the board's decision.

Source: Reuters
